images.title: Keep only two turns
images.purpose: Show a four armed figure whose top arm bends right and bottom arm bends left: a half turn fits but a quarter turn does not.
images.composition: Three copies of the figure in one row with wide gaps: start, after a half turn, after a quarter turn.
images.exact_structure: Three copies of one figure in a row, each with 4 arms in a plus shape and a centre dot, in teal #0072B2. In the start copy the top arm is reddish purple #CC79A7 and bends right at its end, the bottom arm bends left, and the left and right arms are straight. Copy 2 is turned 180 degrees and looks identical to the start. Copy 3 is turned 90 degrees clockwise, so its bent arm lands on the right arm position and the figure differs. Exactly 3 figures.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
all four arms bending the same way
images.takeaway: Opposite arms alike and neighbours different keeps only the half turn and the full turn.
images.description: Three copies of a four armed figure: the start, the half turned copy which matches, and the quarter turned copy which does not.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to follow the red arm and say why the half turn fits but the quarter turn does not.

image_decisions.why: Keeping only two turns is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
